sanskrit: brahmādīnāṃ khecarāṇāṃ kṣitau ca; ye cādhastāt saṃvasante narendra tatraiva tad darśanaṃ darśayan vai; samyak kṣemyaṃ ye pathaṃ saṃśritā vai
english: To Brahmā and the rest, to the sky-faring ones, O lord of men, and to those who dwell upon the earth and in the realms below — to all of them he revealed this very vision, that auspicious vision granted to those who have taken to the path that leads aright.

sanskrit: sāṃkhyāḥ sarve sāṃkhyadharme ratāś ca; tadvad yogā yogadharme ratāś ca ye cāpy anye mokṣakāmā manuṣyās; teṣām etad darśanaṃ jñānadṛṣṭam
english: All the followers of Sāṃkhya who delight in the Sāṃkhya discipline, and likewise the Yogins who delight in the discipline of Yoga, and whatever other men there are who long for liberation — for them this vision is the one seen through knowledge.

sanskrit: jñānān mokṣo jāyate pūruṣāṇāṃ; nāsty ajñānād evam āhur narendra tasmāj jñānaṃ tattvato 'nveṣitavyaṃ; yenātmānaṃ mokṣayej janmamṛtyoḥ
english: From knowledge is liberation born for men; from ignorance there is none — so they declare, O lord of men. Therefore knowledge is to be sought in its very truth, by which one may free the self from birth and death.

sanskrit: prāpya jñānaṃ brāhmaṇāt kṣatriyād vā; vaiśyāc chūdrād api nīcād abhīkṣṇam śraddhātavyaṃ śraddadhānena nityaṃ; na śraddhinaṃ janmamṛtyū viśetām
english: Having gained knowledge from a brāhmaṇa or a kṣatriya, from a vaiśya or a śūdra, even from a lowly man, the believer must ever and constantly hold it in faith; into the man of faith birth and death shall not enter.

sanskrit: sarve varṇā brāhmaṇā brahmajāś ca; sarve nityaṃ vyāharante ca brahma tattvaṃ śāstraṃ brahmabuddhyā bravīmi; sarvaṃ viśvaṃ brahma caitat samastam
english: All the classes are brāhmaṇas, all are sprung from Brahman, and all forever utter Brahman. The truth, the teaching, I declare with a mind fixed on Brahman: this whole universe, in its entirety, is Brahman.

sanskrit: brahmāsyato brāhmaṇāḥ saṃprasūtā; bāhubhyāṃ vai kṣatriyāḥ saṃprasūtāḥ nābhyāṃ vaiśyāḥ pādataś cāpi śūdrāḥ; sarve varṇā nānyathā veditavyāḥ
english: From the mouth of Brahman the brāhmaṇas were brought forth, from the arms the kṣatriyas were brought forth, from the navel the vaiśyas, and from the feet the śūdras; all the classes are to be understood thus and not otherwise.

sanskrit: ajñānataḥ karmayoniṃ bhajante; tāṃ tāṃ rājaṃs te yathā yānty abhāvam tathā varṇā jñānahīnāḥ patante; ghorād ajñānāt prākṛtaṃ yonijālam
english: Out of ignorance they resort, O king, to this or that womb whose source is karma, and so pass into nothingness; even so the classes, bereft of knowledge, fall — out of dread ignorance into the natural web of wombs.

sanskrit: tasmāj jñānaṃ sarvato mārgitavyaṃ; sarvatrasthaṃ caitad uktaṃ mayā te tasthau brahmā tasthivāṃś cāparo yas; tasmai nityaṃ mokṣam āhur dvijendrāḥ
english: Therefore knowledge is to be sought on every side; it abides everywhere, as I have told you. Brahman stands fast, and that other one who likewise stands fast — for him the chief of the twice-born declare eternal liberation.

sanskrit: yat te pṛṣṭaṃ tan mayā copadiṣṭaṃ; yāthātathyaṃ tad viśoko bhavasva rājan gacchasvaitadarthasya pāraṃ; samyak proktaṃ svasti te 'stv atra nityam
english: What you asked, that I have taught according to its very truth; be free of sorrow, O king. Reach the far shore of this matter. It has been rightly declared — may all be well with you herein for ever.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca sa evam anuśāstas tu yājñavalkyena dhīmatā prītimān abhavad rājā mithilādhipatis tadā
english: Bhīṣma said: Thus instructed by the wise Yājñavalkya, the king, the lord of Mithilā, was then filled with joy.

sanskrit: gate munivare tasmin kṛte cāpi pradakṣiṇe daivarātir narapatir āsīnas tatra mokṣavit
english: When that best of sages had departed, after the circumambulation had been performed, the king Daivarāti, knower of liberation, sat there.

sanskrit: gokoṭiṃ sparśayām āsa hiraṇyasya tathaiva ca ratnāñjalim athaikaṃ ca brāhmaṇebhyo dadau tadā
english: He caused ten million cows to be touched in gift, and likewise gold, and a single handful of gems besides he then bestowed upon the brāhmaṇas.

sanskrit: videharājyaṃ ca tathā pratiṣṭhāpya sutasya vai yatidharmam upāsaṃś cāpy avasan mithilādhipaḥ
english: And having established the kingdom of Videha upon his son, the lord of Mithilā lived on, devoting himself to the discipline of the renunciant.

sanskrit: sāṃkhyajñānam adhīyāno yogaśāstraṃ ca kṛtsnaśaḥ dharmādharmau ca rājendra prākṛtaṃ parigarhayan
english: Studying the knowledge of Sāṃkhya and the science of Yoga in its entirety, and condemning, O lord of kings, both dharma and adharma as belonging to mere nature,

sanskrit: anantam iti kṛtvā sa nityaṃ kevalam eva ca dharmādharmau puṇyapāpe satyāsatye tathaiva ca
english: holding the eternal and the absolute alone to be endless, he reckoned dharma and adharma, merit and demerit, the true and the false alike,

sanskrit: janmamṛtyū ca rājendra prākṛtaṃ tad acintayat brahmāvyaktasya karmedam iti nityaṃ narādhipa
english: and birth and death too, O lord of kings, as belonging to nature; thus he meditated ever, O ruler of men: this is the work of the Unmanifest, of Brahman.

sanskrit: paśyanti yogāḥ sāṃkhyāś ca svaśāstrakṛtalakṣaṇāḥ iṣṭāniṣṭaviyuktaṃ hi tasthau brahma parātparam nityaṃ tam āhur vidvāṃsaḥ śucis tasmāc chucir bhava
english: The Yogins and the Sāṃkhyas, defined each by their own teaching, behold it thus: severed from the welcome and the unwelcome, Brahman stands, higher than the highest. The wise call it eternal and pure; therefore be pure.

sanskrit: dīyate yac ca labhate dattaṃ yac cānumanyate dadāti ca naraśreṣṭha pratigṛhṇāti yac ca ha dadāty avyaktam evaitat pratigṛhṇāti tac ca vai
english: Whatever is given and whatever is received, what is bestowed and what is approved, and what a man gives, O best of men, and what he accepts — it is the Unmanifest alone that gives this, and the Unmanifest that receives it.

sanskrit: ātmā hy evātmano hy ekaḥ ko 'nyas tvatto 'dhiko bhavet evaṃ manyasva satatam anyathā mā vicintaya
english: For the Self alone is the one Self; who other than yourself could be greater than you? Think thus continually; do not ponder it otherwise.

sanskrit: yasyāvyaktaṃ na viditaṃ saguṇaṃ nirguṇaṃ punaḥ tena tīrthāni yajñāś ca sevitavyāvipaścitā
english: He by whom the Unmanifest is not known — whether with its qualities or beyond all qualities — by that unwise man holy fords and sacrifices must be frequented.

sanskrit: na svādhyāyais tapobhir vā yajñair vā kurunandana labhate 'vyaktasaṃsthānaṃ jñātvāvyaktaṃ mahīpate
english: Not by recitations, nor by austerities, nor by sacrifices, O joy of the Kurus, does one attain abidance in the Unmanifest; only by knowing the Unmanifest, O lord of the earth.

sanskrit: tathaiva mahataḥ sthānam āhaṃkārikam eva ca ahaṃkārāt paraṃ cāpi sthānāni samavāpnuyāt
english: Likewise one may attain the station of the Great Principle, and the station born of egoity, and the stations that lie even beyond egoity.

sanskrit: ye tv avyaktāt paraṃ nityaṃ jānate śāstratatparāḥ janmamṛtyuviyuktaṃ ca viyuktaṃ sad asac ca yat
english: But those, devoted to the scriptures, who know the eternal that is beyond the Unmanifest — that which is free of birth and death, and free of both being and non-being —

sanskrit: etan mayāptaṃ janakāt purastāt; tenāpi cāptaṃ nṛpa yājñavalkyāt jñānaṃ viśiṣṭaṃ na tathā hi yajñā; jñānena durgaṃ tarate na yajñaiḥ
english: This I obtained of old from Janaka, and he in turn obtained it, O king, from Yājñavalkya. Knowledge is supreme; sacrifices are not its equal. By knowledge one crosses the hard passage, not by sacrifices.

sanskrit: durgaṃ janma nidhanaṃ cāpi rājan; na bhūtikaṃ jñānavido vadanti yajñais tapobhir niyamair vrataiś ca; divaṃ samāsādya patanti bhūmau
english: Birth and death are a hard passage, O king, and yield no abiding good — so say the knowers of knowledge. By sacrifices, austerities, observances, and vows men reach heaven, only to fall again to earth.

sanskrit: tasmād upāsasva paraṃ mahac chuci; śivaṃ vimokṣaṃ vimalaṃ pavitram kṣetrajñavit pārthiva jñānayajñam; upāsya vai tattvam ṛṣir bhaviṣyasi
english: Therefore worship that which is supreme, great, pure, gracious, the spotless and hallowed liberation, O knower of the field-knower. Worshipping, O king, the sacrifice of knowledge and the truth, you shall become a seer.

sanskrit: upaniṣadam upākarot tadā vai; janakanṛpasya purā hi yājñavalkyaḥ yad upagaṇitaśāśvatāvyayaṃ tac; chubham amṛtatvam aśokam ṛcchatīti
english: This secret doctrine Yājñavalkya then imparted of old to King Janaka — that by which, when the eternal and imperishable is reckoned and known, one attains the auspicious, sorrowless state of immortality.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca aiśvaryaṃ vā mahat prāpya dhanaṃ vā bharatarṣabha dīrgham āyur avāpyātha kathaṃ mṛtyum atikramet
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Having won great lordship, O bull of the Bharatas, or wealth, or having gained a long span of life — how then may one pass beyond death?

sanskrit: tapasā vā sumahatā karmaṇā vā śrutena vā rasāyanaprayogair vā kair nopaiti jarāntakau
english: By great austerity, by action, by sacred learning, or by the application of elixirs — by what means does one escape old age and death?

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca atrāpy udāharantīmam itihāsaṃ purātanam bhikṣoḥ pañcaśikhasyeha saṃvādaṃ janakasya ca
english: Bhīṣma said: On this too they recount an ancient tale — the dialogue here of the mendicant Pañcaśikha with Janaka.

sanskrit: vaideho janako rājā maharṣiṃ vedavittamam paryapṛcchat pañcaśikhaṃ chinnadharmārthasaṃśayam
english: Janaka, king of Videha, questioned the great seer Pañcaśikha, foremost knower of the Vedas, who had cut away every doubt concerning dharma and the goal of life.

sanskrit: kena vṛttena bhagavann atikrāmej jarāntakau tapasā vātha buddhyā vā karmaṇā vā śrutena vā
english: By what course of conduct, O blessed one, might one pass beyond old age and death — by austerity, by understanding, by action, or by sacred learning?

sanskrit: evam uktaḥ sa vaidehaṃ pratyuvāca parokṣavit nivṛttir naitayor asti nānivṛttiḥ kathaṃ cana
english: Thus addressed, the knower of the unseen replied to the king of Videha: there is no halting these two, nor is there any way to keep them from halting all else.

sanskrit: na hy ahāni nivartante na māsā na punaḥ kṣapāḥ so 'yaṃ prapadyate 'dhvānaṃ cirāya dhruvam adhruvaḥ
english: For the days do not turn back, nor the months, nor again the nights; this fleeting creature sets out upon the long, unending road.

sanskrit: sarvabhūtasamucchedaḥ srotasevohyate sadā uhyamānaṃ nimajjantam aplave kālasāgare jarāmṛtyumahāgrāhe na kaś cid abhipadyate
english: The destruction of all beings is borne along forever as if by a current; and as he is swept along and sinks in the boatless ocean of time, where old age and death are the great sea-monster, no one comes to his aid.

sanskrit: naivāsya bhavitā kaś cin nāsau bhavati kasya cit pathi saṃgatam evedaṃ dārair anyaiś ca bandhubhiḥ nāyam atyantasaṃvāso labdhapūrvo hi kena cit
english: No one shall belong to him, nor does he belong to anyone; this gathering with wife and other kinsfolk is but a meeting upon the road. No lasting companionship has ever yet been won by anyone.

sanskrit: kṣipyante tena tenaiva niṣṭanantaḥ punaḥ punaḥ kālena jātā jātā hi vāyunevābhrasaṃcayāḥ
english: Begotten by time, born again and again, they are flung this way and that, groaning over and over — like masses of cloud driven by the wind.

sanskrit: jarāmṛtyū hi bhūtānāṃ khāditārau vṛkāv iva balināṃ durbalānāṃ ca hrasvānāṃ mahatām api
english: For old age and death are the devourers of beings, like two wolves — of the strong and the weak, of the small and the great alike.

sanskrit: evaṃbhūteṣu bhūteṣu nityabhūtādhruveṣu ca kathaṃ hṛṣyeta jāteṣu mṛteṣu ca kathaṃ jvaret
english: When beings are of such a nature, ever coming to be yet never enduring, how should one rejoice when they are born, and how burn with grief when they die?

sanskrit: kuto 'ham āgataḥ ko 'smi kva gamiṣyāmi kasya vā kasmin sthitaḥ kva bhavitā kasmāt kim anuśocasi
english: Whence have I come, who am I, where shall I go, and to whom do I belong? In what do I abide, where shall I be? Wherefore, and over what, do you grieve?

sanskrit: draṣṭā svargasya na hy asti tathaiva narakasya ca āgamāṃs tv anatikramya dadyāc caiva yajeta ca
english: For there is no one who has beheld heaven, nor likewise hell; yet without transgressing the sacred tradition one should give gifts and offer sacrifice.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca aparityajya gārhasthyaṃ kururājarṣisattama kaḥ prāpto vinayaṃ buddhyā mokṣatattvaṃ vadasva me
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: O best of the royal seers of the Kurus, without forsaking the householder's life, who has attained, by his understanding, the discipline of restraint? Tell me the truth of liberation.

sanskrit: saṃnyasyate yathātmāyaṃ saṃnyastātmā yathā ca yaḥ paraṃ mokṣasya yac cāpi tan me brūhi pitāmaha
english: How is this self renounced, and what is he who has renounced the self, and what is the supreme goal of liberation — tell me that, O grandfather.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca atrāpy udāharantīmam itihāsaṃ purātanam janakasya ca saṃvādaṃ sulabhāyāś ca bhārata
english: Bhīṣma said: On this too they recount an ancient tale — the dialogue of Janaka and Sulabhā, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: saṃnyāsaphalikaḥ kaś cid babhūva nṛpatiḥ purā maithilo janako nāma dharmadhvaja iti śrutaḥ
english: There once was a certain king who had won the fruit of renunciation, a man of Mithilā, Janaka by name, known as Dharmadhvaja.

sanskrit: sa vede mokṣaśāstre ca sve ca śāstre kṛtāgamaḥ indriyāṇi samādhāya śaśāsa vasudhām imām
english: Versed in the Veda, in the science of liberation, and in his own kingly science, he held his senses in check and ruled this earth.

sanskrit: tasya vedavidaḥ prājñāḥ śrutvā tāṃ sādhuvṛttatām lokeṣu spṛhayanty anye puruṣāḥ puruṣeśvara
english: Hearing of that virtuous conduct of his, the wise who know the Veda, and other men throughout the worlds, looked upon him with longing, O lord of men.

sanskrit: atha dharmayuge tasmin yogadharmam anuṣṭhitā mahīm anucacāraikā sulabhā nāma bhikṣukī
english: Now in that righteous age a certain wandering mendicant woman named Sulabhā, who practised the discipline of Yoga, was roaming over the earth.

sanskrit: tayā jagad idaṃ sarvam aṭantyā mithileśvaraḥ tatra tatra śruto mokṣe kathyamānas tridaṇḍibhiḥ
english: As she wandered through all this world, she heard the lord of Mithilā spoken of, here and there, by the triple-staffed ascetics in their discourse on liberation.

sanskrit: sā susūkṣmāṃ kathāṃ śrutvā tathyaṃ neti sasaṃśayā darśane jātasaṃkalpā janakasya babhūva ha
english: Having heard the most subtle account, but in doubt whether it was true or not, she conceived a resolve to behold Janaka in person.

sanskrit: tataḥ sā viprahāyātha pūrvarūpaṃ hi yogataḥ abibhrad anavadyāṅgī rūpam anyad anuttamam
english: Then, casting off her former shape by the power of Yoga, the faultless-limbed one took on another, surpassing form.

sanskrit: cakṣur nimeṣamātreṇa laghvastragatigāminī videhānāṃ purīṃ subhrūr jagāma kamalekṣaṇā
english: In the mere blink of an eye, moving with the swiftness of a flying arrow, the fair-browed, lotus-eyed woman came to the city of the Videhas.

sanskrit: sā prāpya mithilāṃ ramyāṃ samṛddhajanasaṃkulām bhaikṣacaryāpadeśena dadarśa mithileśvaram
english: Reaching lovely Mithilā, thronged with prosperous folk, on the pretext of seeking alms she came to behold the lord of Mithilā.

sanskrit: rājā tasyāḥ paraṃ dṛṣṭvā saukumāryaṃ vapus tathā keyaṃ kasya kuto veti babhūvāgatavismayaḥ
english: Beholding her surpassing delicacy and her form, the king was struck with wonder: Who is this, whose is she, and whence?

sanskrit: tato 'syāḥ svāgataṃ kṛtvā vyādiśya ca varāsanam pūjitāṃ pādaśaucena varānnenāpy atarpayat
english: Then, bidding her welcome and assigning her an excellent seat, he honoured her with water for her feet and gratified her with choice food.

sanskrit: atha bhuktavatī prītā rājānaṃ mantribhir vṛtam sarvabhāṣyavidāṃ madhye codayām āsa bhikṣukī
english: Then, having eaten and well pleased, the mendicant woman challenged the king — surrounded by his ministers, in the midst of all who were skilled in disputation.

sanskrit: sulabhā tv asya dharmeṣu mukto neti sasaṃśayā sattvaṃ sattvena yogajñā praviveśa mahīpate
english: But Sulabhā, in doubt whether he was truly liberated in his observances or not, being skilled in Yoga, entered his being with her own being, O lord of the earth.

sanskrit: netrābhyāṃ netrayor asya raśmīn saṃyojya raśmibhiḥ sā sma saṃcodayiṣyantaṃ yogabandhair babandha ha
english: Joining the rays of her eyes to the rays of his eyes, she bound him, as he was about to challenge her, with the bonds of Yoga.

sanskrit: janako 'py utsmayan rājā bhāvam asyā viśeṣayan pratijagrāha bhāvena bhāvam asyā nṛpottamaḥ
english: And King Janaka, smiling, discerning her intent, the best of kings, met her purpose with his own purpose.

sanskrit: tad ekasminn adhiṣṭhāne saṃvādaḥ śrūyatām ayam chatrādiṣu vimuktasya muktāyāś ca tridaṇḍake
english: Let this dialogue now be heard, set within one and the same seat — between him who, though amid parasol and the rest, was liberated, and her who was liberated within the triple staff.

sanskrit: bhagavatyāḥ kva caryeyaṃ kṛtā kva ca gamiṣyasi kasya ca tvaṃ kuto veti papracchaināṃ mahīpatiḥ
english: "Where, lady, has this wandering of yours been undertaken, and where will you go? Whose are you, and whence?" — thus the lord of the earth questioned her.

sanskrit: śrute vayasi jātau ca sadbhāvo nādhigamyate eṣv artheṣūttaraṃ tasmāt pravedyaṃ satsamāgame
english: "In learning, in age, and in birth, true worth is not discerned; therefore in these matters an answer must be made known when the good come together.

sanskrit: chatrādiṣu viśeṣeṣu muktaṃ māṃ viddhi sarvaśaḥ sa tvāṃ saṃmantum icchāmi mānārhāsi matā hi me
english: Know me to be wholly liberated, despite the parasol and such distinctions. I wish to take counsel with you, for you are deemed by me worthy of honour.

sanskrit: yasmāc caitan mayā prāptaṃ jñānaṃ vaiśeṣikaṃ purā yasya nānyaḥ pravaktāsti mokṣe tam api me śṛṇu
english: From whom of old I gained this distinctive knowledge, of whose teaching on liberation there is no other expounder — hear of him too from me.

sanskrit: pārāśaryasagotrasya vṛddhasya sumahātmanaḥ bhikṣoḥ pañcaśikhasyāhaṃ śiṣyaḥ paramasaṃmataḥ
english: Of the aged, great-souled mendicant Pañcaśikha, of the lineage of Parāśara, I am the most esteemed disciple.

sanskrit: sāṃkhyajñāne tathā yoge mahīpālavidhau tathā trividhe mokṣadharme 'smin gatādhvā chinnasaṃśayaḥ
english: In the knowledge of Sāṃkhya, in Yoga, and in the rule of kings, and in this threefold law of liberation, he had traversed the whole path and cut away every doubt.

sanskrit: sa yathāśāstradṛṣṭena mārgeṇeha parivrajan vārṣikāṃś caturo māsān purā mayi sukhoṣitaḥ
english: Wandering forth by the path laid down in the scriptures, he once dwelt happily with me for the four months of the rainy season.

sanskrit: tenāhaṃ sāṃkhyamukhyena sudṛṣṭārthena tattvataḥ śrāvitas trividhaṃ mokṣaṃ na ca rājyād vicālitaḥ
english: By that foremost of Sāṃkhyas, who had clearly seen the truth, I was instructed in the threefold liberation according to its very essence, yet was not swayed from my kingdom.

sanskrit: so 'haṃ tām akhilāṃ vṛttiṃ trividhāṃ mokṣasaṃhitām muktarāgaś carāmy ekaḥ pade paramake sthitaḥ
english: So I, freed of passion, follow that whole threefold way joined to liberation, moving alone, established in the supreme station.

sanskrit: vairāgyaṃ punar etasya mokṣasya paramo vidhiḥ jñānād eva ca vairāgyaṃ jāyate yena mucyate
english: Dispassion, again, is the supreme rule of this liberation; and dispassion is born of knowledge alone, by which one is set free.

sanskrit: jñānena kurute yatnaṃ yatnena prāpyate mahat mahad dvaṃdvapramokṣāya sā siddhir yā vayotigā
english: By knowledge one makes the effort, and by effort the great is attained; the great leads to release from the pairs of opposites — that perfection which transcends the passing of age.

sanskrit: seyaṃ paramikā buddhiḥ prāptā nirdvaṃdvatā mayā ihaiva gatamohena caratā muktasaṅginā
english: This supreme wisdom, this freedom from the pairs of opposites, has been won by me even here, as I move with delusion gone and attachment cast off.

sanskrit: yathā kṣetraṃ mṛdūbhūtam adbhir āplāvitaṃ tathā janayaty aṅkuraṃ karma nṛṇāṃ tadvat punarbhavam
english: As a field made soft and flooded with water brings forth the sprout, so does the action of men bring forth rebirth.

sanskrit: yathā cottāpitaṃ bījaṃ kapāle yatra tatra vā prāpyāpy aṅkurahetutvam abījatvān na jāyate
english: And as a seed scorched in a potsherd, set down anywhere, though it has the capacity to sprout, is no longer seed and does not sprout,

sanskrit: tadvad bhagavatā tena śikhāproktena bhikṣuṇā jñānaṃ kṛtam abījaṃ me viṣayeṣu na jāyate
english: even so, by that blessed mendicant whom Pañcaśikha taught, my knowledge has been made seedless, and amid the objects of sense it sprouts no more.

sanskrit: nābhiṣajjati kasmiṃś cin nānarthe na parigrahe nābhirajyati caiteṣu vyarthatvād rāgadoṣayoḥ
english: It clings to nothing — neither to harm nor to possession — nor does it take delight in these, since passion and its faults are seen to be in vain.

sanskrit: yaś ca me dakṣiṇaṃ bāhuṃ candanena samukṣayet savyaṃ vāsyā ca yas takṣet samāv etāv ubhau mama
english: He who should anoint my right arm with sandal, and he who should hack at my left with an axe — these two are alike to me.

sanskrit: sukhī so 'ham avāptārthaḥ samaloṣṭāśmakāñcanaḥ muktasaṅgaḥ sthito rājye viśiṣṭo 'nyais tridaṇḍibhiḥ
english: Happy am I, my purpose accomplished, regarding clod and stone and gold alike; free of attachment, seated upon my throne, I surpass the other triple-staffed ascetics.

sanskrit: mokṣe hi trividhā niṣṭhā dṛṣṭā pūrvair maharṣibhiḥ jñānaṃ lokottaraṃ yac ca sarvatyāgaś ca karmaṇām
english: For in liberation a threefold ground has been seen by the great seers of old: knowledge that transcends the world, and the utter renunciation of all actions —

sanskrit: jñānaniṣṭhāṃ vadanty eke mokṣaśāstravido janāḥ karmaniṣṭhāṃ tathaivānye yatayaḥ sūkṣmadarśinaḥ
english: Some men, versed in the science of liberation, declare it grounded in knowledge; while others, ascetics of subtle vision, declare it grounded in action.
